title: Tab Sunset List
user: Knowledge workers with chronic browser-tab overload who need a low-friction way to turn stale tabs into deliberate keep, schedule, bookmark, or close decisions.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN thread asks directly how people handle browser tab overload; responses include closing tabs or using specialized tools.
Firefox iOS is asked to expose tab groups arriving from synced desktop devices, showing that even native tab grouping does not resolve cross-device tab accumulation.

recurrence: A direct user question and an independent browser feature request in the same month show that unmanaged tabs remain a cross-device utility problem.
current_workaround: Keep everything open, bulk-close tabs, create tab groups, or move important pages into bookmarks/read-later services.
incumbents_and_gap: Native tab groups, OneTab, Workona, and session managers store tabs; the unresolved gap is a deliberate expiry queue that asks for a decision after a chosen age and preserves a compact rationale.
smallest_useful_product: A browser extension that tags tabs with an expiry date and decision type, presents a daily small review queue, and exports kept items to browser bookmarks or Markdown. Non-goals: a new browser, cloud sync, AI summaries, or replacing native session restore.
success_measure: Among weekly active pilots, median open-tab count falls 30% after four weeks while at least 80% of explicitly saved tabs remain retrievable.
monetization: free — the minimal browser utility gains trust without a cloud account; optional one-time cross-browser export could follow.
constraints: Use only tabs/bookmarks permissions needed; never send browsing history off device; make close actions undoable while browser APIs allow it.
why_distinct: It uses time-bounded decisions and exportable outcomes, rather than treating tab hoarding as a storage or workspace-management problem.
